newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends up on power unit outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends up on power unit outages.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures finished higher Wednesday on news of power unit outages in the U.S. West and some forecasts of hot weather in the U.S. West over the longer term, industry sources said.
"There was talk of these outages through the market all day," said one Western electricity trader.

August Palo Verde (PV) ended up 61 cents at $36.06 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $36.45 and trading as low as $35.85, while September settled up 62 cents at $30.15 following exchanges at $29.80-30.25 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds finished between 20 cents lower and 40 cents higher.

August California Oregon Border (COB) closed nine cents higher at $23.33 after trades at $23.25-$23.70, while September finished 14 cents higher at $23.09 following trades in a range of $23.00-23.40 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds ended up between 15 and 40 cents.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 832 PV and 568 COB contracts had traded.

Western physical power prices and futures values were said to be strong based on transmission problems on the Pacific Intertie, some forecasts of warm weather in the Southwest and Western generation unit outages, sources said.

In generation news, the 750 megawatt (MW) unit 5 at the Four Corners coal-fired power plant in New Mexico will be shut Friday for three weeks, the plant's operator, Arizona Public Service Co (APS), said Wednesday.
The unit needs work to repair a ground, or dead spot, in its high pressure generator field, the spokesman said.
Four Corners' other 750 MW unit plus a 245 MW unit and two 185 MW units were said to be operating normally.
Restarts of the 1,070 MW unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 at the San Onofre Nuclear Generating (SONG) Station, in San Clemente, Calif., were set for July 15 and July 17.

Also, the 1,073 MW unit 2 at the Diablo Canyon nuclear power plant was expected to remain at 75 percent power Wednesday pending results of further analysis and monitoring, plant operator Pacific Gas & Electric Co said.
No information was available as to how long the unit, located at Avila Beach on California's central coast, would continue to operate at the curtailed level.
Power production at the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state was still around 15 percent of capacity as of early Wednesday, with the unit expected to be on line later this week.
The 750 MW Mohave coal-fired unit 2 in Nevada, which tripped off line Monday due to a tube leak, was scheduled to restart today.

Separately, capacity on the AC segment of the Pacific Intertie will be trimmed by 250 MW to 3,200 MW between 0800 and 1800 PDT Thursday and by 450 MW between 0900 and 1600 Friday for maintenance, a spokeswoman for the Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) said.
Meteorologists called for cool, wet weather to linger over the Pacific Northwest into the weekend, followed by warmer, drier conditions next week.

Forecasters were split on their outlook for the Southwest. Some expected arid, seasonal weather to stay in the region through next week, while others predicted very hot weather stretching from California to much of Midwest.
((--Chris Reese, New York Power Desk +1 212 859 1627))
